verdict: NOT ACCEPTED. All 43 English-to-Hebrew pairs are semantically correct and the Hebrew 23 omission is a genuine gap in the source's English, but three things block acceptance: the variant note is not integrated, the tomekh paragraph/page_start encoding is wrong, and change logs and open-question lists in candidate-round5 are stale.

alignment_findings.note: Each English sentence renders its Hebrew stanza: homage/walk/girds strength; casting away idols / herald (Elijah); falsehood (חנף) / house of the proud; walks in my midst; nations and kingdoms confounded; scroll and book / those who wait (חוכיו); princely tread (Esau's tears); lowly / yoke of the kingdom; wandering of five hundred years.

s263 lines 8–10: 'As to Bel set on a throne, over what does he reign? Through whom was he crowned that he has hastened to reign?' is a single printed stanza. The two questions render עַל מֶה מָלָךְ and הֲלֹא בְּמִי נִמְלָךְ. כִּי אָץ לִמְלוֹךְ. The regex chunks 10 and 11 are a split at the '?' and do not reflect a source division. The joined pairing is right.

umillifnei (Before any king), umah (Molech), zakh (Pure One), zer (garland), chiddeshu (renews realm), chovesh (healing), torach (oppression of kingdoms), tohar (purity of merits / floods), yahav (lay burden), yaavru (like angels / ‘The Lord will reign’), kittim, kevod. All match.

alignment_findings.note: s266 lines 2–4 print לְכָל גֹּבַהּ יַפִּיל… וּכְאוֹר זָרוּעַ יִמְלֹךְ. On s267 the English goes straight from kevod ('…when He completes His work and will reign.') to 'He will fold up the skies…', which renders לְרָאִי יַקְפִּיל / וַחֲדָשִׁים יַכְפִּיל / פּוּר הִפִּיל / מִצִּיּוֹן, i.e. He24. Nothing on s267 renders casting down heights, lowering mountain and hill, or darkening nations. The omission is real, and leaving en null with a source note and no substitute translation is correct.

leroi, matu, malkhu (דְגוּיִם = fish), nedivei, niggun, sikkut (Sikkut/Kiyun), sod, izzuz, al_rum, pur, pachad (shofar three times), tzevi, tzevaot, qetzinim, qeruim, raz, roeh (Teman/Gilead), shinan (Shinanim), sheiyyot, tekhan, tomekh. All match. Shinan's English 'assembly of angels' renders the main-text reading וְסוֹד פְּלִיאִיּוֹת, not the variant.

The following splits match the scans. Hebrew: kittim at כֵּס מַמְלַכְתּוֹ. | יִכּוֹן (s264→s266); sikkut at כִּיּוּן | גִּלּוּלִים (s266→s268); qetzinim at יַשְׁלִיכוּ. | קוֹל (s268→s270). English: gilyon at 'ways of life,' | 'open' (s261→s263); zakh at 'vengeance' | 'and reigns.' (s263→s265); kittim at 'established and' | 'He will reign.' (s265→s267); sikkut at 'abominations' | 'of Kiyun' (s267→s269); qetzinim at 'The princes' | 'who once ruled' (s269→s271).

The last word on s262, זֵר (at the end of the יֹאחֵז דַּרְכּוֹ line), is a catchword: s264 begins again with זֵר בְּשַׁלְּכוֹ. Excluding it from the text is right, and zer starts on s264 with page_start true. No other page transition in this unit has a catchword: s264→s266, s266→s268 and s268→s270 all run straight on.

The small קהל. at the right margin before אַנְסִיכָה on s260 is a correct speaker placement before stanza 1. The alignment label 'קהל' drops the printed period that the candidate block 'קהל.' keeps; make them match the print. The small ח׳ before תּוֹמֵךְ on s270 is correctly attached before the tomekh stanza. The English has no speaker labels, which is correct.

On s270 the Hebrew תּוֹמֵךְ begins a new indented paragraph: the line after בְּמָלְכוֹ יִמְלֹךְ: is left short, and the next line is indented with ח׳. The English on s271 also starts a new paragraph with the cue תומך. The alignment gives the English tomekh paragraph 2 but the Hebrew tomekh paragraph 1.

Hebrew tomekh (s270) has page_start true, but it is mid-page: s270 starts with קוֹל יִתְּנוּ. English tomekh (s271) has page_start true, but s271 starts with 'who once ruled'. Elsewhere page_start marks the first fragment on a scan. Here it appears to have been used to mark a paragraph start.
